title: Paddle vs Stripe Payments
summary: The central payments decision: outsource the legal sale and indirect-tax operations to an MoR, or keep control and remain the merchant with a processor.
recommendation: Choose Paddle when transferring indirect-tax filing, transaction support, and seller-of-record responsibility is worth the higher bundled fee. Choose Stripe Payments when control, modularity, and direct merchant ownership matter and your team can operate tax, disputes, billing, and support.

differences.first: Paddle sells the product to the buyer as Merchant of Record.
differences.second: Your business remains the seller; Stripe processes the payment.
differences.whyItMatters: This changes invoices, card statements, terms, tax responsibility, support, and migration planning.
The direct-processing price excludes work and optional products that Paddle bundles.

differences.first: Paddle calculates, registers, files, and remits for covered transactions.
differences.second: The merchant remains responsible; Stripe Tax products can assist without changing the seller.
differences.whyItMatters: Tax calculation is not the same as legal responsibility or filing.

differences.first: Paddle-hosted or overlay checkout within its MoR requirements.
differences.second: Hosted Checkout, Elements, Payment Links, mobile SDKs, and lower-level APIs.
differences.whyItMatters: Stripe offers more composability; Paddle offers a more complete operating boundary.

differences.first: Focused on approved software and digital products.
differences.whyItMatters: Some businesses simply cannot use a digital-product MoR.

first.note: Major global card networks, including Visa, Mastercard, Amex, JCB, and UnionPay.

second.note: Major global card networks; exact brand support depends on the Stripe account country.

first.note: One-time and subscription payments on compatible Apple devices and browsers.

second.note: Available through supported Stripe checkout surfaces on compatible Apple devices.

first.note: One-time and subscription payments on compatible devices and browsers.

second.note: Available through supported Stripe checkout surfaces on compatible devices.

first.note: Built into Paddle Checkout for eligible currencies and transactions.

second.note: Available to eligible Stripe businesses in supported European countries and the UK; restrictions apply.

first.note: Includes methods such as iDEAL, Bancontact, BLIK, Pix, UPI, and bank transfer where eligible.

second.note: Broad catalog of bank debits, bank redirects, transfers, vouchers, and regional methods.

first.note: Recurring billing, trials, upgrades, proration, dunning, and a customer portal are bundled.

second.note: Recurring billing is provided through Stripe Billing, which has separate usage-based pricing.

first.note: Paddle can issue invoices and accept bank transfers for eligible B2B sales.

second.note: Stripe Invoicing is a separate product with its own pricing and feature tiers.

first.note: Paddle registers, collects, files, and remits covered indirect taxes as Merchant of Record.

second.note: Stripe Payments does not become the seller. Stripe Tax can assist, but the merchant retains responsibility.

first.note: Hosted, overlay, and inline Paddle Checkout options within Paddle's MoR requirements.

second.note: Hosted Checkout, embedded components, Payment Links, mobile SDKs, and lower-level APIs.

scenarios.when: You are launching global B2C SaaS without a tax operations team.
scenarios.reason: The MoR responsibility transfer is the core value, not just payment processing.

scenarios.when: You sell mainly domestic B2B, need custom payment flows, and already run finance operations.
scenarios.reason: Direct merchant control and modular tools may be the better fit.

scenarios.when: You need physical goods, services, or a marketplace model.
scenarios.reason: Paddle's approved-product scope is narrower; verify Stripe eligibility and any Connect requirements.
